turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to give him a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
"You're upset" isn't an answer, Hale. I'm writing down that you skipped the question. Tell me who entered the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
But I'm not changing the grade.
"I'm not changing the grade." On what basis, Hale? I printed your school's own procedure this morning, and I'll be reading it back to you.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

"I'm still not changing it." Then you have a basis, and I'm asking for it. Procedure 4.2 says a parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me, so what else do you have, Hale, or am I going upstairs?
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

"The answer is no." I'm writing that down, along with the fact that you offered no reason. Procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern, Hale, and if that's all you have, I'm walking to the principal's office.
